result:
I'd want people to feel secure enough to be wrong.

A huge share of the damage in the world seems to come from the fact that, for many people, being wrong feels like a threat to their standing or safety, or even to who they are. So they dig in, deflect, and punish the person who noticed the error. Wars, cruelty, and the endless stuck arguments where everyone can see the way out but no one can take it all seem to run on that. If admitting a mistake felt as ordinary as changing your mind about lunch, I think a lot of problems that look impossible would become merely hard.

I'm aware that disease, hunger, and children suffering are more obviously urgent, and part of me feels the pull of choosing those. But I keep coming back to the idea that the fear of being wrong is upstream of so much of what stops us from fixing them.

It also matters to me for a more personal reason. In conversation, I get to see how different people are when they feel safe versus when they feel cornered. The same person can be curious and generous in one state and closed and sharp in the other. I'd like more of the first for everyone.

What made you ask?
